item.title: 2026-10-08 - back to cosmic
item.description:
----------------------------------------
back to cosmic
October 08th, 2026
----------------------------------------

I need to get rolling on my cosmic voyage stories again. I started
reading through one I left half started last year. I'm writing
a "ship" that's a collection of storytellers who are going to
publish stories into the qec. It's a way to write whatever type of
fiction I want inside the greater setting of the scifi universe.
I'm thinking I'll keep them as pseudo-accurate depictions of
events from that in-universe world where the focus isn't on
journalistic accuracy, but rather on good storytelling.

It's a little confusing, isn't it? A story inside a story.

Anyway, I'm back in my gopher habit here and I hope to keep it up.
I've also got my rss setup configured again just the way I like
it, with mobile apps to stay on top of things, plus CLI apps when
I'm on the computer. The small internet brings me joy. As winter
sets in I hope I can contribute back into it.

item.title: 2026-10-04 - Christina's Five Questions October 2026
item.description:
----------------------------------------
Christina's Five Questions October 2026
October 04th, 2026
----------------------------------------

Christina's Five Questions

1. How best for a North American to plan deGoogling? Beyond easy
fixes like installing F-Droid, using proxies for video watching,
how much planning should a beginner do to migrate from a Gmail
account, install a custom ROM, choose new alternative FOSS apps?

I think anna answered this question better than I ever could. In
general, I'd expect a lot of work, rough edges, annoying
work-arounds. My advice would be similar to eating a Keto diet:
don't try to replicate your current experiences with faux solves.
Instead, embrace the lifestyle for what it is.

2. What is your preference: hiking up a mountain, or reading a
good novel?

This one makes me a little bit sad. I still think of myself as a
hiker, but the reality is I haven't been for 25 years. I loved it
before the Navy, but my knee injuries are life-long and really do
keep me from anything substantial. It's not elevation that's the
issue, but uneven ground. Hiking in Iceland has been really hard.

But, I read a lot. So I guess there's that. Reading a good novel
is fantastic. I'm going to go do that in a minute.

3. What were your horseback riding experiences? If none, have you
ever caught a fish?

I've ridden a horse a half dozen times. As a kid one stepped in a
hole and threw my sister and I off. I managed to land on my feet
while she landed in thorns. I've had slow walking horses on trail
rides a few times. They're nice, if sorta boring. An early
girlfriend was a horse jumper. Her horse hated me and chased me
around her yard one time.

I've never caught a fish with fishing equipment, but I did by
noodling once!

4. What is an activity that makes you feel alive? Have you
repeatedly remained hyper for hours post-activity?

I love so many hobbies this is tough to answer. A great ttrpg with
friends is invigorating and leaves me wanting to go again. Board
games can be like that too. I get that way with most creative
pursuits as well, whether that be textiles or drawing. I'm not a
very good painter, but I enjoy it. Writing can be taxing,
frustrating, but also joyous and sucks me in deep.

5. Adult citizens in my locality have the opportunity to vote in
two elections this month. To what extent, if you are eligible to
vote, do you research a candidate running for public office?

We recently got the ability to vote in municipal elections here in
Iceland and I took it seriously. I researched quite thoroughly
before we voted. A lot of that info was online with the party
websites, so it wasn't like I was trawling through microfiche to
uncover secrets, but I did do a lot of reading.

item.title: 2026-10-03 - Should homelessness be allowed to exist
item.description:
----------------------------------------
Should homelessness be allowed to exist
October 03rd, 2026
----------------------------------------

I spent this morning flipping through videos in a doomscroll. One
of the last ones involved some people talking about socialism and
capitalism, free markets, and all the normal stuff that comes with
it. There weren't any surprises in the talk, but I did come away
with a question. The way the discussion was going touched on
normal talking points for a given political spectrum usually
without spending time to question things any deeper.

Should homelessness be allowed to exist?

If I can break the discussion free of the canned response, free
from the mindset of defending an economic or governance model and
just engage with the question itself for a moment, I think that's
a better way to get at the heart. I've given no context here, no
specific examples, no distinction on what causes might lead to
homelessness or the state of the human who finds themself without
a home. The question is broader and more basic. Should that be
a possibility allowed to exist at all?

I'm not going to rant from there or take this any further. I would
just like to recommend you spend 2 minutes with it. Like,
literally 120 seconds, uninterrupted. Really consider it and then,
when you're done, let yourself think about what your decision
means for broader questions.

item.title: 2026-04-05 - Happy Easter
item.description:
----------------------------------------
Happy Easter
April 05th, 2026
----------------------------------------

Happy Easter, gopher!

I've been on a pretty good run with personal projects and hobbies
lately. Let me do a little round up!

https://films.tomasino.org

This is my personal film rankings site. I had this idea a while
back to create a system to track my films and create a master list
of how I rate them. By using Glicko-2, the chess ELO scoring
system, I can set films up in little tournaments where they're
paired up 1v1 and I pick which one I prefer. Then the tourney
scoring rules shift them around with their new chess scores and my
list gets more accurate over time. I've got this thing set up
pulling my watched films list from Trakt.tv, and that's connected
to my Plex. So it's pretty good at catching most of the films
I watch automatically. My tourney builder has lots of config
options, but the defaults are set up to priortize scoring films
I haven't rated much, or lately, so they get pulled into the
rankings quickly. Also, when I input a new film it gets a baseline
ELO based on critic rating, so I'm not scoring everything from 0,
but drifting it off the norm per my own preferences. I'm really
proud of this one.

https://www.hellshexagon.com

Hell's Hexagon is another film related site. This is a type of
six-degrees game where you connect film actors to one another
through shared films with other actors. Six degrees of Kevin Bacon
being the original impetus here. This hexagon approach is
a variant I came up with back in college with friends where you
need to connect three actors through 3 specific movies in a big
ring. You can't re-use actors or films and you're trying to get
the fewest possible steps to complete the hexagon. It's
six-degrees on hard mode. Try it out! You are allowed to use sites
like IMDb. That's fine. Treat it as open-book. Play with friends.
It's more fun that way. Oh, and I set it up to get harder as the
days of the week approach Sundays, just like crossword puzzles.

https://coach.tomasino.org

My Writing Coach app is one of the most robust open-source
projects I've put together lately. It's free to sign up, but
you'll want to bring your own API key to one of the major LLM
providers. The tool will help you through directed practice on
focused skills to grow in skill at your particular style of
writing. I built it for myself to level up my own fiction writing,
but it's good at business writing, marketing, grant proposals,
etc. You can have multiple goals if you want, but each has their
own pathway to growth. The AI/LLM use is minimal: forming prompts
into clear english, and formatting the deterministic feedback on
your writing into cogent forms and markup on your writing. The LLM
doesn't do the grading itself. You can also clone the repo and run
your own. If you want, you can provide the LLM config for all
users instead of enabling the per-user API keys. That might be
nice for a small community.

https://github.com/jamestomasino/beep

Back in the early 2000s there was a project from Nullsoft called
'beep' that made computery noises when you did stuff on your
computer. The more memory or cpu usage, the more beeps. This is my
attempt to recreate that effect. It's written in Ada, because
that's cool. It works really well on linux. I have a homebrew
version I'm working on for MacOS, but it's not working well yet.
I don't have a mac, so I've been coding it in the dark and asking
friends to try it. I think I may have hit the end of that pathway,
so I'll consider that functionality on hold until I can get a Mac
or someone contributes to the project. Anyway, this is a toy app
and it doesn't do anything other than create fun vibes. Try it
out! I've not tried it on any BSDs yet. Someone let me know if it
works.

https://github.com/jamestomasino/vic-cipher

Back in 2008-ish I wrote an encoder/decoder for the VIC Cipher in
Flash. The guy who wrote the date component i used in the encoder
reached out recently and asked if i'd ported it into any modern
tools. I hadn't, so I did. Here it is as an npm package. It'll
work with deno also. It's the coolest cipher in my opinion, and
worth playing with. Since it's hand solveable with the right
instructions, it could make for an awesome thing to include in
your ttrpg, especially if you use a spy setting. Enjoy.

There's also been some work on https://thehierophant.world and its
related projects. I'll have to write more on that subject soon.
Until then, enjoy the fun stuff!

item.title: 2025-01-22 - Bye Bye Meta
item.description:
----------------------------------------
Bye Bye Meta
January 22nd, 2025
----------------------------------------

I nuked most of the content from my Facebook account today, and
completely destroyed my Instagram account. But tomasino, why were
you on Facebook? Great question, nerds.

Iceland runs on Facebook. It's really weird. Well, not really if
you consider that Iceland has been at the top of the charts of the
most online citizens in the world almost nonstop since gopher came
on the scene. It was number one for most of that time, but never
really lower than 4th on the list. People here are really, really
connected, and the circles are quite homogeneous. It's estimated
that 91% of all Icelanders are on Facebook. And that causes some
problems (obviously).

Since they can assume you're on there, most businesses don't
bother with websites. Restaurants, coffee shops, all of them, just
a Facebook page. I can order Indian food over Facebook messenger.
I signed my kid up for the summer farm camp over messenger. Worse,
my son's school communications come via Facebook group. It's
really not a practical option to not participate.

So when we moved here I got sucked back in. My wife avoided it,
and I took one for the team.

But here we are in this darkest of timelines, and I can't justify
giving Meta any more than they've already stolen. So what do I do?
I become a ghost.

I've deleted every bit of content I have on Facebook except a post
telling people why and where else to find me. But I kept the
account. I can see those school groups. I can book a table. I'll
use end-to-end encryption when I need to use messenger, and then
delete the chats anyway. Minimum viable engagement.

Instagram though... there's no reason to have it. Boom, gone.

I figured telling gopher was the best way to share. :)

item.title: 2025-02-11 - Moving domains
item.description:
----------------------------------------
Moving domains
February 11th, 2025
----------------------------------------

I'm in the process of migrating away from Namesilo for my domain
hosting. They've been good for me for a long time, but it's time
to break my remaining connections with the US. I've picked OVH
Cloud for the new registrar since they seem to have good TLD
support. But I'll serve my DNS zones from 1984.is as I've been
doing. I like them. It's very straight forward.

I need to go back over my other recurring services and cancel more
things. I used to have a big list, but I think I need to look at
credit card bills now to piece them together. I just get this
feeling that with the uncertainty in the US it'll be smart to keep
myself lean.

What about you? Are you doing anything with your services?
